takeaway: The Hering-Breuer reflex prevents overinflation of the lungs via stretch receptors; peripheral chemoreceptors (carotid bodies) respond mainly to low PO2.

question.text: Which of the following regarding the regulation of respiration is correct?
question.say: Which of the following regarding the regulation of respiration is correct?

answer.text: The Hering–Breuer reflex prevents overinflation of the lungs.
answer.say: The Hering Breuer reflex prevents overinflation of the lungs.

lines.text: Breathing is conducted by the brain stem, in the pons and the medulla.
Stretch receptors in the lungs send signals back to the brain stem.
When a lung is stretched too far, it is in danger of overinflation.
Then the Hering-Breuer reflex blows the whistle and stops the inflation.
Lungs protected: that is the correct statement.
Remember too, peripheral chemoreceptors in the carotid bodies respond mainly to low oxygen, and in part to pH.
